                  xy_constrained=True,
                  apply_selfweight=False, max_sw_to_area_ratio=10.,
                  tol_v_X_diff=1e-5, tol_v_ta_diff=1e-4,
                  min_k=3, max_k=10, 
                  disp=False, **kwargs):
    """
    Performs an iterative form-finding process using the Force Density Method (FDM) with optional self-weight considerations.

    Args:
        CWG (object): An object representing the constrained geometry.
        e_q (torch.Tensor, optional): A tensor representing force densities for each edge.
        v_z (torch.Tensor, optional): A tensor of z-coordinate adjustments for vertices.
        v_ta_0 (torch.Tensor, optional): A tensor representing initial tributary areas for self-weight.
        v_P_live (torch.Tensor, optional): A tensor representing live external forces on vertices.
        xy_constrained (bool, optional): Whether to constrain the solution to the xy-plane. Defaults to True.
        apply_selfweight (str, optional): Specifies how self-weight should be applied ('dynamic', 'init', or None). Defaults to 'dynamic'.
        max_selfweight_fac (float, optional): Maximum factor for self-weight adjustments. Defaults to 10.
        tol_v_X_diff (float, optional): Convergence tolerance for vertex displacement differences. Defaults to 1e-5.
        tol_v_ta_diff (float, optional): Convergence tolerance for self-weight differences. Defaults to 1e-4.
        min_k (int, optional): Minimum number of iterations. Defaults to 3.
        max_k (int, optional): Maximum number of iterations. Defaults to 10.
        disp (bool, optional): If True, prints detailed progress during iterations. Defaults to False.
        update (bool, optional): If True, updates the original geometry with the results. Defaults to True.
        **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments for customization.

    Returns:
        DataObject: A result object containing updated geometry and force densities after solving.
    """

    if apply_selfweight in [None, False, 'init']:
        min_k, max_k = 1, 1

    v_X_0           = v_X if v_X is not None else CWG.feat.v[('x', 'y', 'z')]

    # process loading
    if v_P is None:
        v_P         = CWG.feat.v['px', 'py', 'pz']
    elif v_P is not None and v_P.size(1) == 1:
        v_P         = th.cat((th.zeros_like(v_X_0[:, :2]), v_P[:, 2:]), dim=-1) 

    if apply_selfweight:
        # process stablising upper limit of applied load
        g_area_xy_0     = CWG.geom_area_xy()
        g_sw_max        = g_area_xy_0 * max_sw_to_area_ratio

    if disp:
        print('...[Iterative FDM]...')

    # force density processing
    if e_q is None:
        e_q = CWG.feat.e.q
    ee_q = e_q

    if e_q.size(0) == CWG.n_ee:
        e_q = th.zeros((CWG.n_e, 1), device=CWG.device)
        e_q[CWG.feat.e._is_edge.flatten()] = ee_q
    elif e_q.size(0) == CWG.n_e:
        ee_q = e_q[CWG.feat.e._is_edge]
    else:
        raise RuntimeError('Unknown size of e_q given...')

    k = 0
    while True:
        # LOADING CONDITION

        # COMPUTE LOADS
        v_Pff = th.zeros_like(v_X_0)
        if apply_selfweight:
            v_sw                = CWG.verts_tributary_areas(v_X_0) 
            g_sw                = v_sw.sum()
            # self-weight stabliser
            g_sw_mul = 1.0 
            if max_sw_to_area_ratio is not None:
                g_sw_           = min(g_sw, g_sw_max)  
                g_sw_mul        = g_sw_ / g_sw
            v_sw_ff = th.zeros_like(v_X_0)
            v_sw_ff[:, 2:3] = - v_sw * g_sw_mul
            v_Pff += v_sw_ff

        v_Pff += v_P

        # SOLVE EQUATION
        v_X_1 = _fdm(CWG, ee_q, v_X_0, v_Pff)

        v_X_diff = (th.linalg.norm(v_X_1.detach() - 
                    v_X_0, dim=1)**2).mean()
        if disp:
            print('..k: {}, Δv_x: {:3f}'.format(k, v_X_diff.detach().item())) 

        k += 1
        if k >= min_k and \
           ((v_X_diff < tol_v_X_diff) or k >= max_k):
            break

        v_X_0 = v_X_1

    # calculate discrepency between selfweight
    v_sw_diff = th.tensor(0., device=CWG.device)
    if apply_selfweight:
        v_sw_diff = (v_sw[CWG.vis_freed] - v_sw_ff[CWG.vis_freed]).sum()
        if disp:
            print('v_sw_diff: {}'.format(v_sw_diff))

    # update information
    CWG.feat.v[('x', 'y', 'z')] = v_X_1
    CWG.feat.v[('pffx', 'pffy', 'pffz')] = v_Pff
    CWG.feat.e.q    = e_q
    CWG.feat.e._l   = CWG.edges_lengths()
    CWG.feat.e._f   = CWG.feat.e._l * e_q

def check_horizontal_equilibrium(CWG, mode='e_fxy', rtol=1e-3):
    """
    Checks the horizontal force equilibrium by computing residual forces in the xy-plane.

    Args:
        CWG (object): The graph object containing nodes and edges.
        mode (str, optional): The force mode to use when calculating edge forces. Defaults to 'e_fxy'.
        rtol (float, optional): Relative tolerance for evaluating the equilibrium. Defaults to 1e-3.

    Returns:
        None: Prints the mean of the residual forces for free vertices in the xy-plane.
    """
    v_is_frd        = ~CWG.feat.v.is_fixed
    e_is_e          = CWG.feat.e._is_edge

    v_Xxy           = th.cat((CWG.feat.v[('x', 'y')], CWG.feat.v.zero), dim=1)
    v_Pxy           = CWG.feat.v.zero.repeat(1, 3)

    e_fxy           = CWG.edges_forces_xy(mode=mode)

    v_Rxy           = compute_vertices_residuals(CWG, v_Xxy, v_Pxy, e_fxy, e_is_e)
    v_Rxy_mn_freed  = v_Rxy[v_is_frd.flatten()].mean()
    print("Vertices residual forces (xy): {}".format(v_Rxy_mn_freed.detach().item()))

def check_vertical_equilibrium(CWG, rtol=1e-3):
    """
    Checks the vertical force equilibrium by computing residual forces along the z-axis.

    Args:
        CWG (object): The graph object containing nodes and edges.
        rtol (float, optional): Relative tolerance for evaluating the equilibrium. Defaults to 1e-3.

    Returns:
        None: Prints the mean of the residual forces for free vertices along the z-axis.
    """
    v_is_freed = ~CWG.feat.v.is_fixed
    e_is_edge = CWG.feat.e._is_edge

    v_X = CWG.feat.v[('x', 'y', 'z')]
    v_P = CWG.feat.v.zero.repeat(1, 3)
    v_P[:, 2:] = - CWG.verts_tributary_areas()
    e_f = CWG.feat.e._f

    v_R = compute_vertices_residuals(CWG, v_X, v_P, e_f, e_is_edge)
    v_R_mn_freed = v_R[v_is_freed.flatten()].mean()
    print("Vertices residual forces: {}".format(v_R_mn_freed.detach().item()))

@local_scope_handler
def compute_vertices_residuals(CWG, v_X, v_P, e_f, e_is_e=None):
    """
    Computes the residual forces at vertices by taking into account edge forces and external forces.

    Args:
        CWG (object): The graph object containing nodes (vertices) and edges.
        vX (torch.Tensor): Tensor representing the coordinates of the vertices.
        vP (torch.Tensor): Tensor representing external forces applied to the vertices.
        eF (torch.Tensor): Tensor representing the forces along the edges.
        e_is_edge (torch.Tensor, optional): Boolean tensor indicating active edges. If None, all edges are considered active.

    Returns:
        torch.Tensor: Tensor representing the residual forces at each vertex.
    """
    e_f = e_f.clone()

    CWG.nodes['v'].data['X'] = v_X
    # render load as 3d vectors
    if len(v_P.shape) == 1 or v_P.shape[1] == 1:
        v_P = F.pad(v_P, (2, 0))

    # ignore forces of inactive edge
    e_is_e = (e_is_e.reshape(-1, 1) if e_is_e is not None \
              else th.ones_like(e_f)).to(v_X.device, dtype=th.bool)
    e_f[~e_is_e] = 0.

    CWG.nodes['v'].data['v_P'] = v_P
    CWG.update_link_data(ntype='e', feat=e_f, ltype=('v', 'e', 'v'), update_nodes=True)
    CWG.update_link_data(ntype='e', feat=e_is_e, ltype=('v', 'e', 'v'), update_nodes=True)

    CWG.apply_links(fn.u_sub_v('X', 'vev_dX'), etype=('v', 'e', 'v'))
    CWG.apply_links(fn.e_normalize('vev_dX', 'vev_dX_normed'), etype=('v', 'e', 'v'))
    CWG.update_all(fn.e_prod(['e_f', 'e_is_e', 'vev_dX_normed'], 'mail_vev_F'),
                   fn.sum('mail_vev_F', 'v_rX'), etype=('v', 'e', 'v'))
    CWG.apply_node(fn.sum)
    r_vF = CWG.nodes['v'].data['v_rF']
    return r_vF

def dr_torch(
    CWG,
    kmax: int = 10000,
    dt: float = 1.0,
    tol1: float = 1e-3,
    tol2: float = 1e-6,
    c: float = 0.1,
    rk_steps: Literal[1, 2, 4] = 2,
    callback: Callable = None,
    callback_args: list = None,
):
    """Implementation of the dynamic relaxation method using PyTorch."""

    # Validate callback
    if callback and not callable(callback):
        raise ValueError("The provided callback is not callable.")

    coeff = Coeff(c)
    ca = coeff.a
    cb = coeff.b

    # Extract input data
    v_X = CWG.feat.v['x', 'y', 'z'] #indata.vertices  # m
    P = CWG.feat.v['px', 'py', 'pz'] #indata.loads  # kN
    free = CWG.vis_free #indata.free
    e_q_pre = CWG.feat.e.q_pre  #indata.e_q_pre
    e_l_pre = CWG.feat.e.l_pre #indata.e_l_pre  # kN
    e_f_pre = CWG.feat.e.f_pre #indata.e_f_pre  # m
    e_l_init = CWG.feat.e.l_init #indata.e_l_init  # m
    E = CWG.feat.e.E #indata.E  # kN/mm2 => GPa
    radius = CWG.feat.e.r #indata.radius  # mm
    C = CWG.C # #indata.C  # Sparse matrix, should be PyTorch sparse tensor
    Ct = C.transpose(0, 1)
    Ci = C[:, free]
    Cit = Ci.transpose(0, 1)

    # Material properties
    A = 3.14159 * radius**2  # mm^2
    EA = E * A  # kN

    # Initial values
    e_q = CWG.feat.e.q_0  #indata.q0
    e_l = CWG.feat.e.l_0  #indata.l0  # noqa: E741
    e_f = e_q * e_l
    v_X = CWG.feat.v['x', 'y', 'z']   #indata.v0
    v_R = CWG.feat.v.zero.repeat(1,3)     #indata.r0

    if th.all(e_l_init == 0):
        e_l_init = e_l ##indata.l0

    # Helper function for RK integration
    def rk(x0, v0, steps=2):
        def acceleration(t, v):
            dx = v * t
            x[free] = x0[free] + dx[free]
            r[free] = p[free] - th.matmul(D, x)
            return cb * r / mass

        if steps == 1:
            return acceleration(dt, v0)

        if steps == 2:
            B = [0.0, 1.0]
            K0 = dt * acceleration(K[0][0] * dt, v0)
            K1 = dt * acceleration(K[1][0] * dt, v0 + K[1][1] * K0)
            dv = B[0] * K0 + B[1] * K1
            return dv

        if steps == 4:
            B = [1.0 / 6.0, 1.0 / 3.0, 1.0 / 3.0, 1.0 / 6.0]
            K0 = dt * acceleration(K[0][0] * dt, v0)
            K1 = dt * acceleration(K[1][0] * dt, v0 + K[1][1] * K0)
            K2 = dt * acceleration(K[2][0] * dt, v0 + K[2][1] * K0 + K[2][2] * K1)
            K3 = dt * acceleration(K[3][0] * dt, v0 + K[3][1] * K0 + K[3][2] * K1 + K[3][3] * K2)
            dv = B[0] * K0 + B[1] * K1 + B[2] * K2 + B[3] * K3
            return dv

        raise NotImplementedError

    # Start iterating
    for k in range(kmax):
        q_e_f_pre = e_f_pre / l
        q_e_l_pre = f / e_l_pre
        q_EA = EA * (l - e_l_init) / (e_l_init * l)

        # Handle inf and NaN
        q_e_l_pre = th.where(th.isinf(q_e_l_pre) | th.isnan(q_e_l_pre), th.zeros_like(q_e_l_pre), q_e_l_pre)
        q_EA = th.where(th.isinf(q_EA) | th.isnan(q_EA), th.zeros_like(q_EA), q_EA)

        q = e_q_pre + q_e_f_pre + q_e_l_pre + q_EA
        D = th.matmul(th.matmul(Cit, th.diag(q.flatten())), C)
        mass = 0.5 * dt**2 * th.matmul(Ct, e_q_pre + q_e_f_pre + q_e_l_pre + EA / e_l_init)

        # RK integration
        x0 = x.clone()
        v0 = ca * v.clone()
        dv = rk(x0, v0, steps=rk_steps)
        v[free] = v0[free] + dv[free]
        dx = v * dt
        x[free] = x0[free] + dx[free]

        # Update
        u = th.matmul(C, x)
        l = normrow(u)
        f = q * l
        r = p - th.matmul(Ct, th.matmul(th.diag(q.flatten()), u))

        # Compute convergence criteria
        crit1 = th.linalg.norm(r[free])
        crit2 = th.linalg.norm(dx[free])

        # Callback
        if callback:
            callback(k, x, crit1, crit2, callback_args)

        # Check for convergence
        if crit1 < tol1:
            break
        if crit2 < tol2:
            break

    # Return result
    return ResultData(xyz=x, q=q, forces=f, lengths=l, residuals=r)

def interpolate_2d(X_i, y_i, X_o, 
                   replace_nan=None,
                   setup=None, tol=1e-1):
    """ differentiable  and simplified version of gridspace2d"""

    #TODO: handle points outside: snap to corners, or segment
    dvc = X_i.device

    # if idx == -1
    # identify pts outside of simplices

    # create mask
    # find their closest point to boundary
    # replace X_o with closest points
    # find relevant indices for replaced X_o
    # -when saving weights for reuse, also include mask, and relevant indices
    # interpolate
    if setup:
        tri, smpx, idx = setup
    else:
        tri, smpx, idx = setup_interpolate_2d(X_i, y_i, X_o, tol)

    has_nan = (idx < 0).sum().item() > 0
    if not replace_nan:
        assert not has_nan
    # else:
    #     n_data = X_i.shape[0]
    #     n_smpx = smpx.shape[0]
    #     smpx = th.cat(smpx, th.tensor([n_smp]).to(dvc))

    y_i_ = y_i[smpx[idx]].reshape(idx.shape[0], 3)
    X_i_ = X_i[th.tensor(tri.simplices).to(dvc, th.long)]

    d_Xo_to_tri = X_i_[idx] - X_o.unsqueeze(1)
    d_Xo_to_tri = F.pad(d_Xo_to_tri, pad=(0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0))

    Xo_tri_areas = th.norm(th.cross(d_Xo_to_tri[:, [0, 1, 2], :], 
                              d_Xo_to_tri[:, [1, 2, 0], :], dim=-1), dim=-1)
    Xo_tri_areas_sum = Xo_tri_areas.sum(-1, keepdim=True)
    w = Xo_tri_areas / Xo_tri_areas_sum

    # actual interpolation
    y_o = (y_i_[:, [2, 0, 1]] * w).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
    if replace_nan and has_nan:
        if isinstance(replace_nan, (int, float)):   
            y_o[y_i] = replace_nan
        elif callable(replace_nan):
            y_o = replace_nan(X_i, y_i, X_o, y_o, idx)

    return y_o

@reduction_decorator
def root_mean_pth_power_error(actual, predicted, p=2):
    """Calculate the root of the mean p-th power error between actual and predicted."""
    errors = th.pow(th.abs(actual - predicted), p)
    mean_errors = th.mean(errors, dim=-1)  # Compute mean across features, not batch
    return th.pow(mean_errors, 1/p)

def generate_filterwise_directions(model, seed=None):
    """
    Generate filter-wise normalized random directions for a given model,
    storing perturbations layer by layer, see [Visualizing the Loss Landscape of Neural Nets](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.09913).

    Args:
        model (torch.nn.Module): The model whose parameters define the normalization.
        seed (int, optional): Random seed.

    Returns:
        dict: Two dictionaries (delta, eta) with filter-normalized directions for each parameter.
    """
    if seed is not None:
        th.manual_seed(seed)

    delta = {}
    eta = {}

    for name, param in model.named_parameters():
        if "weight" in name:  # Only normalize weights
            # Generate random directions
            delta_param = th.randn_like(param)
            eta_param = th.randn_like(param)

            # Calculate norms
            if param.dim() == 2:
                norm_delta = param.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True)
                norm_eta = param.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True)
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unexpected parameter dimension: {param.dim()}")

            # Avoid division by zero
            norm_delta = th.where(norm_delta == 0, th.tensor(1.0, device=param.device), norm_delta)
            norm_eta = th.where(norm_eta == 0, th.tensor(1.0, device=param.device), norm_eta)

            # Apply normalization
            delta_param = delta_param / (delta_param.view(param.size(0), -1).norm(dim=1, keepdim=True) + 1e-8)
            delta_param = delta_param * norm_delta
            eta_param = eta_param / (eta_param.view(param.size(0), -1).norm(dim=1, keepdim=True) + 1e-8)
            eta_param = eta_param * norm_eta

            # Store results
            delta[name] = delta_param
            eta[name] = eta_param
        else:  # Store zeros for non-weight parameters
            delta[name] = th.zeros_like(param)
            eta[name] = th.zeros_like(param)

    return delta, eta

def perturb_model_weights(model, delta, eta, alpha, beta, deepcopy=True):
    """
    Apply filter-wise perturbations to the model weights.

    Args:
        model (torch.nn.Module): The model to perturb.
        delta (dict): Layer-wise perturbation directions (delta).
        eta (dict): Layer-wise perturbation directions (eta).
        alpha (float): Scaling factor for delta.
        beta (float): Scaling factor for eta.
        deepcopy (bool, optional): If True, the model is copied before perturbation.

    Returns:
        torch.nn.Module: Perturbed model.
    """
    if deepcopy:
        perturbed_model = copy.deepcopy(model)
    else:
        perturbed_model = model

    for name, param in perturbed_model.named_parameters():
        if name in delta:
            param.data += alpha * delta[name] + beta * eta[name]

    return perturbed_model

torch + gnn/gdl + graph + autodiff + archi/struct/geom forward/inverse form-finding 😊

Your one-stop general auto-differentiable library for form-finding reticulated/discrete systems.

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: Welcome to the installation guide for compas_torch_fofin. To ensure a smooth installation process, please follow the steps below.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
compas_torch_fofin requires the following dependencies:

  • PyTorch
  • DGL (Deep Graph Library)

Warning

Both PyTorch and DGL require specific configurations depending on your system (e.g., CUDA version if you have a GPU). As a result, these cannot be automatically installed as part of the package dependencies and must be installed manually.

docs.title: 1. (Optional, Recommended) Create a Virtual Environment
docs.text:
To avoid conflicts with other Python packages and to maintain a clean working environment, we highly recommend creating a new Python virtual environment.

For instance, with Conda: 

conda create -n compas_torch_fofin_env python=3.9
conda activate compas_torch_fofin_env
conda install pip

docs.title: 2. Install PyTorch
docs.text:
Visit the PyTorch Installation Guide to find the correct command for your system. We recommend PyTorch 2.3.0 (newer versions will require installing DGL from source).

For example, if using CUDA 11.8:

pip install torch==2.3.0+cu118 torchvision==0.15.0+cu118 torchaudio==2.3.0+cu118 -f https://download.pytorch.org/whl/torch_stable.html

docs.title: 3. Install DGL
docs.text:
Install the latest pip-installable version of DGL (2.2.1) using the following command:

pip install dgl==2.2.1

Alternative: Install from Source

Optionally, to use newer versions of DGL (or PyTorch), you must build it from source. Follow the instructions in the DGL Installation Guide for detailed steps.

docs.title: 4. Install compas_torch_fofin
docs.text:
Install the compas_torch_fofin package via pip:

pip install compas_torch_fofin

docs.title: 5. Verify the Installation
docs.text:
To verify the installation, open Python and run the following:

import compas_torch_fofin

If no errors occur you have succesfully installed compas_torch_fofin.
